title: Screenreader announcer and sequence preservation for cost rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Improve assistive technology behavior when dynamic rollout cards and cost toggles change state in the Console. Problem: when rollout states or cost metrics update in-place (canary -> primary, metric values refresh, or region fallback), screen readers may read items out of order or not announce the new state clearly. This causes confusion for keyboard and screenreader users during deployments and cost investigations. Goals: 1) Provide a robust ARIA announcement strategy so changes to rollout state and cost deltas are reliably communicated. 2) Preserve reading sequence and focus order when list items reflow or are updated, to avoid surprising AT users. 3) Ensure localized numeric formatting and relative change language (e.g., vs previous period) is readable in all supported locales. Deliverables: - Annotated Figma prototype for rollout list and cost row updates (link below). - Design spec with ARIA patterns: use of role="status" for non-interruptive updates, aria-live polite/assertive guidelines per change type, and hidden waveform cues for rapid state toggles. - Keyboard flow diagrams showing how focus is preserved or moved on remove/insert. - i18n phrasing matrix for delta language (en, fr, de, ja, zh) to avoid literal translations that break grammar when combined with numeric suffixes. Acceptance criteria: - Screenreader users hear a concise announcement when a rollout flips from canary to primary ("Canary for Route X promoted to primary") and when cost deltas exceed threshold ("Cost increased 12% this hour"). - When a rollout row is removed due to consolidation, focus moves predictably to the next logical interactive element and a short live region message describes the change. - Numeric formatting uses Intl.NumberFormat for the active locale; tests with fr-FR and ja-JP verify placement of currency, decimal separators, and compact notation. - Keyboard navigation remains linear and does not trap on updates; no focus loss after live updates. Edge cases and trade-offs: - Large tables with continuous updates: we recommend aggregate live summaries (one polite status) rather than announcing every row change to avoid AT noise. - Instant toggles (user-initiated) use assertive announcements; background sync changes use polite/live-hidden banner. - We avoid complex ARIA tree manipulations since some ATs mishandle role=tree; prefer list semantics and explicit tabindex management. Implementation notes for Eng: - Preferred pattern: single dedicated offscreen aria-live region for page-level non-critical updates and per-row aria-live="polite" for row-level important state changes. - Provide data attributes for stable IDs so the DOM reordering can be minimized; prefer visual CSS transforms over DOM removals where possible so ATs preserve sequence. - Include a small experiment flag (feature_x_at_announcements) to toggle assertive vs polite for telemetry. References: - Figma prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/console-rollouts-a11y-proto - Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Console/Rollouts+Accessibility - A11y audit notes: https://docs.redwood.ai/a11y/rollouts-audit-2026 QA checklist: - Manual screenreader passes: NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver + Safari, JAWS + Chrome. - Locale smoke: en-US, fr-FR, de-DE, ja-JP, zh-CN. - Keyboard-only: ensure tab order and logical focus after simulated row insert/remove. - Automated aria-live diff tests using headless AT integration harness. Rollout plan: - Canary: enable for internal orgs and Redwood employees for 1 week. - Metrics to watch: reported confusion incidents, keyboard regression rate, automated AT test failures. Follow-ups: - If aggressive announcements produce noise, revert to aggregated summary pattern. - Explore adding a per-user setting to lower announcement verbosity.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after design-led a11y review of the rollouts list. Attached a narrow-scope prototype that demonstrates three announcement modes: assertive, polite, and aggregated summary.

2026-03-11 - Mateo Ruiz: Reviewed patterns with Eng (runtime team). Dev concerns: excessive DOM churn causes render thrash on lists with 300+ rows. Suggested adding stable data-row-id attributes and only toggle visually when possible.

2026-03-11 - Accessibility Team (Lina Huang): Confirmed recommended use of aria-live for row-level changes and suggested a single status region for aggregate cost deltas. Flagged need for voice phrasing for negative/positive deltas in languages with different sentence order.
2026-03-12 - PM (Ravi Singh): Asked to prioritize fr-FR and ja-JP translations for delta copy due to large customer base in EU and APAC. Also requested telemetry events for announcement counts.
2026-03-12 - Mateo Ruiz: Linked prototype and proposed implementation notes. Will pair with Eng to draft acceptance tests. PR template drafted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/XXXX

2026-03-12 - UX Research (Marina Lopez): Planned quick testing session with 6 keyboard+screenreader participants on 2026-03-16 to validate real-world phrasing and focus behavior. Will report findings as follow-ups.
